title: Optimal Holdout Fraction for Selective Randomization Tests in Two-Stage Enrichment Designs
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 graded the delivered package incremental below the field floor, with the split/count and Fisher-reference transfer not established and no bounded in-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The load-bearing joint split CLT is not reproduced: conditional on a holdout, the complement treatment count g^1 is still random, so the cited fixed-group-proportion complete-randomization CLT cannot be applied directly to (X,R_1).

The Fisher-reference conclusion is asserted by 'the same finite-population argument' after completion B_i+h_s Z_i/sqrt(n), but no conditional split/count CLT or uniform rank/covariance comparison for this random completed population is derived.
The selective transfer and power frontier are plausibly distinct, but the core gives no relevance sentence or theorem-level comparison for several listed closest threads.
DELETE this unconsumed numbered obstruction and its sole supporting def:shrinking-margin-handle, or make it an explicit positioned delivered boundary contribution with a consumer.
proof_attempt_summary: The run built an exact same-cell Fisher reference, a finite-stratum Gaussian optimizer package, and a proposed finite-population sampling/reference transfer. The transfer collapsed because the proof never established a uniform CLT after conditioning on random split counts, studentization, rank perturbation, and the random Fisher-completed population; therefore its finite-population power consequences and downstream interior/branch claims are not established as written. A future re-anchored run must prove that joint conditional permutation theorem first; the exact sharp-null validity proof and the purely Gaussian analytic reductions are the principal reusable pieces.
tldr: For an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set \(S\), a common holdout fraction \(\rho\) indexes a chronological two-stage enrichment randomization and its same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. Stage-one randomized action is the pair of holdout and treatment vectors; this gives a formal specialization of Freidling--Zhao--Gao's augmented-action representation, with their Proposition 1 supplying validity independently of imputability and Proposition 2 supplying computability at the sharp null. A per-array common remainder transfers the shifted sampling cdf and the zero-drift data-dependent reference cdf on every complete signed cell. Finite-product factorization reduces each active cell to a scalar selected Gaussian power. Ehrhard--Borell convexity reduces arbitrary compact positive alternatives to their least coordinate, the sign of \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) fixes the side of the proportional stage weight, all nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, and an explicit two-stratum mixture certifies an interior negative-discrepancy regime. Mixed signs have a complete equality-aware analytic branch characterization, while interval computation returns certified value and optimizer-set boxes and asserts uniqueness only with separation.
gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao establish exact selective randomization inference and explicitly leave holdout allocation and powerful selection-dependent statistics open. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, selective central limit theorems use independent sampling with smooth external randomization, and enrichment-design optimization uses model-based numerical programs. None supplies a design-uniform, array-specific without-replacement transfer that separates the shifted sampling law from the dataset-dependent Fisher reference, or an analytic holdout--weight power frontier.
fill: The project derives the complete signed-cell selected Gaussian limit from a fixed baseline array and the separately indexed local-alternative laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\). For each \(\rho\), it constructs from \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\) the same-design Fisher completion and the exact finite support of quota-respecting candidate histories, recomputes selection for every candidate, retains exactly the observed complete cell, and integrates the ensuing stage-2 kernels. The reference cell probability is an explicit combinatorial sum. A deterministic sampling-cell margin is separated from a random-reference margin stated uniformly in probability. For each admissible baseline array, one common array-dependent modulus controls the sampling-cdf family uniformly over design and alternatives and controls the reference family through an outer supremum of the corresponding sampling probabilities. The required finite-population maximum-influence ratios follow from explicit inequalities using \(M_4\), \(\epsilon\), and positive block shares, and the limiting Gaussian residual variance obeys \(v_j^2\ge\rho\ge\rho_0\); neither is imposed separately. Cross-stratum factorization then yields the scalar selected integrals, which are solved through selected-quantile convexity with the exact chord-equality predicate, inverse-Mills factorization, realizability inequalities, analytic branch exhaustion, and certificate-aware interval computation. The newly maintained pair-spacing condition is realized directly by bounded continuous-density quantile arrays. The negative-discrepancy regime is anchored by deterministic quantiles from an explicit two-component uniform mixture with stated weights, supports, stratum allocations, exact primitive limits, reference-margin convergence, and certified enclosures.
